newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Israel can't bar Arab works in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Israel can't bar Arab works in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian lawmakers rejected on Wednesday an Israeli military order prohibiting workmen from renovating Arab buildings near Jewish enclaves in the heart of the West Bank town of Hebron.

The Palestinian Legislative Council, meeting in the town on Wednesday, said that, since Israel had handed over 80 percent of the town to PLO self-rule earlier this month under a redeployment deal, the army order constituted interference in Palestinian affairs.

"From our side as Palestinians we reject (the Israeli ban), and we are going to continue with the rebuilding in the Old City of Hebron no matter what the reaction from the Israeli side," legislator Zahran Abu Kubeta told Reuters.

Under the order signed by West Bank military commander Uzi Dayan, Israeli forces stopped workmen on Monday from renovating Arab houses in the Old City. The army said Dayan issued the order to protect Jewish settlers in the area.
Israeli soldiers continue to patrol the 20 percent of the city still under their control, a sector where some 400 Jewish settlers and students live among more than 20,000 Palestinians.
Palestinian officials said the order affects 38 apartments in 20 buildings, most of which are now under repair. About 120 apartments are being renovated throughout Hebron's Old City, they said.
"If the Israelis stop the workers, we will face this with all the measures we have at our disposal," Abu Kubeta said.
"There is no possibility of stopping this work."
